fields.corePath: Articleship Planner is for a CA article assistant who is doing three years of articleship and studying for finals at the same time. Step 1, he opens the site and taps Build my plan. Step 2, he enters his articleship start date, his attempt month — May or November — and his firm's busy seasons, which for most firms is September and January. Step 3, he ticks the eight final papers and marks which ones he has already started. Step 4, he taps Generate, and gets a week-by-week plan from today to his attempt, which automatically thins out the study hours in audit season and packs them into the months after. Step 5, he scrolls the plan and taps any week to see the papers and chapters for that week. Step 6, he taps Export my plan as PDF, which is the thing he actually sticks on the wall above his desk and the whole reason the site exists.
fields.knownGaps: Fonts take a moment to load on the first visit and you see the fallback serif flash before Fraunces comes in. The colour scheme is not final — a friend who designs told me the ochre is doing too much work and she is right. The chapter breakdown for Direct Tax is based on the old syllabus in two places, specifically the international taxation chapters, and I need to sit down with the new study material and fix that. On mobile the week cards are cramped: the hours badge and the date run into each other below about 380 pixels and I want to redo that layout properly rather than patch it. There is no way to mark a week as done, so the plan is a fixed artefact rather than something you track against, which two of the article assistants I showed it to asked for immediately. No account either, so if you clear your browser you regenerate the plan from scratch, though that only takes a minute.

notes: Borderline, committed to return on `honest-gaps`. The path is named cleanly, the render confirms every step of it, and there are no placeholders — so five criteria clear. But the student names the PDF export as step 6 and 'the whole reason the site exists', while the live page itself admits the export is beta and sometimes fails, and knownGaps mentions only fonts, colours, syllabus text and mobile spacing. The bar says the gap list must not quietly omit something on the core path. A lenient reviewer could pass this since the page discloses the flakiness in situ; the return is the stricter reading.
